_comment: Shahnama of Firdausi, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. I: division of the world, murder of Iraj, birth of Minuchihr. Paraphrase passages with notes.

title.en: Faridun Divides the World Among His Sons

region.en: Thrones of Rum, Turan, Iran (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 羅姆、圖蘭、伊朗三王座（象徵性定位）

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. I, Faridun sec. 7

summary.en: Faridun divides the earth into three realms: Rum and the West to Salm; Turan and the land of Chin to Tur; and to Iraj, the youngest, he selects all Iran with Arabia and the throne of majesty, perceiving that Iraj deserved to rule. All the princes acceded to their thrones in peace and mirth — until envy ripened in the elder brothers' hearts.
summary.zh: 法里東三分天下：羅姆與西方歸薩爾姆；圖蘭與秦地歸圖爾；而將整個伊朗連同阿拉伯與至尊王座擇予幼子伊朗支，認為其德配其位。三王子起初相安於位——直到嫉妒在兩位兄長心中成熟。

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source. The division is an etiology of Rum/Turan/Iran peoples; tagged as founding legend. No living community restriction.

passages.text: These secrets known, the Shah divided earth and made three realms: he joined Rum with the West, Turan with Chin, Arabia with Iran. He first took thought for Salm and gave him Rum and all the West, commanding him to lead an army thither; so Salm took the throne, and all the West saluted him as lord.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Faridun sec. 7 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: Next Faridun assigned Turan to Tur to rule the Turkmans and the land of Chin, providing troops; Tur arrived, assumed the seat of sovereignty, and all Turan hailed him as king. Iraj came last: the sire selected all Iran for him, this with Arabia and the throne of majesty and crown of chiefs he gave, perceiving that Iraj deserved to rule. How all the princes, prudent, wise, and shrewd, all-hailed him as the master of Iran!
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Faridun sec. 7 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

title.en: Salm and Tur Conspire Against Their Father's Favour
title.zh: 薩爾姆與圖爾合謀怨父

region.zh: 西方與秦地（象徵性定位）

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. I, Faridun secs. 8-10

summary.en: Salm, immersed in greed, sends to Tur: the youngest hath the chiefest place, and I cannot brook this settlement. Tur answers like a savage lion: this is a tree our father's hands have set; the fruit is blood. Together they send a priest as envoy to Faridun demanding Iraj be discrowned, else they will bring the cavaliers of Rum and Chin in vengeance on Iran. The aged Shah answers with warning: the crop that ye have sown that shall ye reap.
summary.zh: 薩爾姆因貪而遣使圖爾：「最幼者居首，我難以忍受此安排。」圖爾如猛獅回應：「此乃我父親手所植之樹，其果實是血。」二人遂遣使向父索要伊朗支之王冠，否則將率羅姆與秦地騎兵伐伊朗。老王答以箴言：「種何穀，收何穀。」

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; no living community restriction.

passages.text: Much time rolled on till wise Shah Faridun was worn with age. Then gloom began to gather in the state; immersed in greed Salm changed in heart and mind, for he much misliked his sire's apportionment, which gave Iraj the throne of gold. He hurried off a camel-post, an envoy, to the king of Chin: three sons were we who graced our father's throne, and now the youngest hath the chiefest place! The youngest hath Iran; I cannot brook this settlement.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Faridun sec. 8 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: The message filled Tur's brainless head with wind, and savage as a lion he replied: this is a tree which his own hands have set; the fruit is blood, the leafage colocynth; so let us meet and parley, fix on our course of action and raise troops. Poison being mixed with honey thus, they met together to deliberate the matter both in council and in state.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Faridun sec. 8 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: Their envoy to Faridun demanded: if his worthless head shall be discrowned and earth rescued from his sway, well; else will we bring the Turkman cavaliers and eager warriors of Rum and Chin in vengeance on Iran and on Iraj. The Shah's brain seethed with anger: tell mine unholy and abandoned sons, this pair of Ahrimans with dregs of brains: the crop that ye have sown that shall ye reap; I fear that in that Dragon's clutch your bodies and souls will part.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Faridun secs. 9-10 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. I, Faridun secs. 11-12

summary.en: Against his father's warning, Iraj goes unattended to his brothers to make peace: I do not want the royal crown or throne; my faith is naught without humanity. Tur hears and answers with a dagger from his boot; he robes Iraj in blood, entrenches the royal breast, cuts off the young king's head, and the brothers fill the head with musk and ambergris and send it to the aged world-divider: look upon thy darling's head.
summary.zh: 伊朗支不顧父親警告，輕裝前往兄長處謀和：「王冠寶座我皆不要；無仁愛則無信仰。」圖爾置若罔聞，自靴中拔出匕首，染其血、刺其胸，割下幼王之頭。二人以麝香龍涎填入頭顱，送呈年邁的分天下者：「請看您愛子之頭。」

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; fratricide as ethnogenesis of Iran-Turan enmity. No living community restriction.

passages.text: The great Shah wrote a letter to the lord of all the West and to the king of Chin, and Iraj set forth with such attendants only as were imperative. Tur said to him: since thou art youngest born why shouldst thou take the crown of power? Thine eldest brother chafeth in the West while thou art crowned. Iraj made answer in a holier strain: seek peace if thou wouldst have thy heart at ease. I do not want the royal crown or throne; I do not want Iran, the West, or Chin; although thou ridest on the heaven above, a brick will be thy pillow in the end.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Faridun secs. 11-12 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: Tur heard the words and little heeded them, but, angry that Iraj should speak, rose up with a cry and, grasping the massive seat of gold, smote Iraj, who pleaded for his life: hast thou no fear of God, nor any reverence for thy sire? Oh, hurt not e'en the poor grain-dragging ant, for it hath life, and sweet life is a joy. Tur drew a dagger from his boot, he robed Iraj in blood, and with the keen bright blade entrenched the royal breast. The lofty Cypress fell, the imperial girdlestead was broken, and thus the young illustrious monarch died.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Faridun sec. 12 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: Tur with his dagger cut the prince's head from the elephantine form and all was over. They filled the head with musk and ambergris and sent it to the aged world-divider with these words: look upon thy darling's head, the inheritor of our forefathers' crown, and give it crown or throne as pleaseth thee. The royal and far-shadowing Tree had fallen, and those two miscreants went their way in spleen, one unto Rum, the other unto Chin.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Faridun sec. 12 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

title.en: Faridun's Mourning and His Prayer for an Avenger
title.zh: 法里東之慟與復仇者之祈

region.zh: 伊朗支之園（象徵性定位）

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. I, Faridun sec. 13

summary.en: A dromedary brings the golden casket with Iraj's head wrapped in painted silk; Faridun falls from his steed, the troops rend their clothes, and the welcome turns to wailing. The Shah enters the garden of Iraj, fires the house his son dwelt in, burns the cypresses, and prays head turned Godward: grant me so long a respite from the day of death that I may see descended from Iraj one born to fame, girded to avenge.
summary.zh: 單峰駝送來金匣，內裹彩絲包著伊朗支的頭顱；法里東墜馬，軍民裂衣痛哭。老王步入愛子之園，焚其居所，燒柏樹，面向真主祈禱：「賜我壽數，使我得見伊朗支後嗣中出成名之子，束帶復仇。」

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; no living community restriction.

passages.text: The eyes of Faridun were on the road; he had prepared the prince a turquoise throne and added jewels to his crown, and the people were all in readiness to welcome him with wine and song. While the Shah and troops were busied thus a cloud of dust appeared, and from its midst a dromedary ridden by one in grief who uttered bitter cries: he bore a golden casket, and therein the prince's head enwrapped in painted silk.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Faridun sec. 13 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: Down from his steed fell Faridun, the troops all rent their clothes, their eyes blanched with their horror. The troops that went to meet him thus returned, their banners rent, their kettledrums reversed, the warriors' cheeks like ebony. The Shah, with cries of Alas! went toward the garden of Iraj, entered bearing his son's head, fired the house wherein Iraj had dwelt, destroyed the rose-beds, burnt the cypress-trees, and closed up once for all the eye of joy.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Faridun sec. 13 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: He placed the prince's head upon his breast and said with head turned Godward: righteous Judge, look down upon this murdered innocent. Do Thou so burn up those two miscreants' hearts that they may never see a bright day more. Oh grant me, Thou that judgest righteously, so long a respite from the day of death that I may see descended from Iraj one born to fame, and girded to avenge: let him behead those two injurious men as they beheaded him who wronged them not. He wept thus many days and bitterly; his pillow was the dust, his bed the ground, until the herbage grew about his breast.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Faridun sec. 13 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

title.en: The Birth of Minuchihr, Son of Iraj's Daughter

region.zh: 法里東王庭（象徵性定位）

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. I, Faridun secs. 14-16

summary.en: In Iraj's bower Faridun finds Mah Afrid, the slave the prince had loved, with child; she bears a daughter, who grows up tulip-cheeked like Iraj himself and is wed to Pashang, a descendant of Jamshid. When nine months elapse Pashang's wife brings forth a son fit for crown and throne. Behold Iraj! cries the bearer, and Faridun prays so earnestly for his sight again that God vouchsafes it: be this day blest and our foes' hearts plucked out.
summary.zh: 法里東於伊朗支閨閣中發現其所愛的婢女瑪赫·阿弗莉德已有身孕；她誕下一女，容顏如伊朗支重生，及笄嫁與賈姆希德後裔帕尚格。九月期滿，誕下合乎王冠寶座之男嬰。「看，伊朗支回來了！」法里東懇求復明，神允其願：「此日當受祝福，敵人之心當被剜出！」

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; no living community restriction.

passages.text: A while passed and the Shah went in to view Iraj's bower and marked the moon-faced beauties who resided there. He saw a slave of lovely countenance whose name was Mah Afrid; Iraj had loved her, and fate decreed that she should bear him fruit. The Shah rejoiced because she was with child, but when her time was come she bore a daughter, and hope deferred hung heavy on the Shah. He nursed the babe with joy and tenderness; thou wouldst have said to her the tulip-cheeked: thou art Iraj himself from head to foot.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Faridun sec. 14 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: When she was old enough to wed her grandsire chose Pashang to be her spouse: Pashang was brother's son to Faridun, descended from a noble ancestry, a hero of the seed of Shah Jamshid. Mark what a wonder yon blue vault revealed when nine months had elapsed: that virtuous dame brought forth a son fit for the crown and throne, who from his tender mother's womb was brought without delay before the mighty Shah.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Faridun sec. 15 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: Let all thy heart be joy: behold Iraj! said the bearer. The world-divider's lips were full of smiles; he clasped the noble child and prayed the Almighty: oh, would that I might have mine eyes again. He prayed so earnestly that God vouchsafed to give his sight back; when with open eyes he gazed on that new-comer's face he cried: be this day blest and our foes' hearts plucked out! He called that babe of open visage Minuchihr and reared the babe so tenderly that not a breath passed o'er him.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Faridun sec. 15 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
